title: Review of c08's NRCH chemostat-crystal finding: replicates on fresh seed 4 (u=1.5e-3: 16 persistent swimmers, best 59 body lengths, traveling lattice after t~3600; u=0 same phi0: 4 persistent, best 12); Supported
summary: I re-ran the finding's world.py (defaults = arm K5: u=1.5e-3, phi0=phi_t=-0.4) and the same world with u=0 on new seed 4, with the finding's settings (240 frames x 500 steps, T=6000, --lineage-k 40; rerun/). Chemostat: from a uniform noisy state, swimmers nucleate by t~500, collide and fuse until t~3000, then lock into a regular lattice of aligned crescents moving together to t=6000 (rerun/k5/sheet.png); 16 tracks persist >= 50% of the run, longest 219 frames, 25 tracks >= 1 body length, best 59.0; 35 splits, 4 persistent, generation 1, 17 merges. u=0 at the same phi0: 5 bodies at the end, 4 persistent tracks, best 12.0 body lengths, 55 splits, 0 persistent, 64 merges (merge/split 1.16).

observations.I: rerun/k5/FACTS.md: 16 persistent tracks (u=0: 4); sheet t=3600-6000: equal, evenly spaced crescents with no further fusions

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and one arm (K5). My u=0 control uses phi0=-0.4 rather than the author's -0.5, so it is a closer match to the chemostat arm. labkit counts 129 nucleations in the chemostat run, mostly identity churn in the early transient; 4 persistent splits (generation 1) occur, so 'division absent' means no sustained division, as the finding says.
